title: Max GCD Sum After Root-Path Cut
statement:
You are given a tree with `n` nodes numbered `1` to `n`, rooted at node `1`. Node `i` holds a positive integer value `A[i]`.

You must choose exactly one node `v` and delete **every node on the path from the root to `v`** (both endpoints included). The remaining nodes split into zero or more connected components. The value of a component is the gcd of the `A` values of all nodes in it, and the score of the choice is the sum of the values of all remaining components. If nothing remains, the score is `0`.

Return the maximum score over all choices of `v`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `A[1], ..., A[n]`.
Each of the next `n - 1` lines contains two integers `u` and `v` (1-indexed), an edge of the tree.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the maximum score.
constraints: The tree has depth at most 5000 when rooted at node 1 (so a recursive DFS stays within limits).

examples.explanation: Node 1 has children 2 and 3; node 3 has children 4 and 5. Choosing v = 1 removes only the root and leaves {2} and {3, 4, 5}: 8 + gcd(18, 6, 9) = 8 + 3 = 11. v = 2 removes {1, 2} and leaves the component {3, 4, 5} with gcd(18, 6, 9) = 3. v = 3 removes {1, 3} and leaves {2}, {4}, {5} with gcds 8 + 6 + 9 = 23. v = 4 leaves {2} and {5}: 8 + 9 = 17. v = 5 leaves {2} and {4}: 8 + 6 = 14. The best is 23.

The root has three leaf children. Choosing v = 1 removes only the root and leaves three single-node components: 4 + 6 + 9 = 19. Choosing a leaf as well removes it too, leaving two components: 15, 13 or 10. The maximum is 19.
The only choice is v = 1, which deletes the whole tree, so nothing remains and the score is 0.

hints: After deleting the root-to-v path, every remaining component is a full subtree hanging off the path: the subtree of a child of some path node, where that child is not itself on the path.
Precompute `G[x]` = gcd of the whole subtree of `x`, and `S[x]` = sum of `G[c]` over the children `c` of `x`.

Let `F[v]` be the score when `v` is chosen. Walking down from the root: `F[root] = S[root]`, and for a child `v` of `p`, `F[v] = F[p] - G[v] + S[v]` (the subtree of `v` is no longer a separate component, but its children's subtrees are). The answer is the maximum `F[v]`.
